market_mood: Hot September inflation has put a Fed rate hike back on the table, which is deepening the AI/tech sell-off even as chip earnings beat, while the Iran war and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia keep energy, shipping and defense in focus.
self_check: My oil and energy calls have been the strongest (77% right) while rate-driven ideas have been near coin-flip, so today leans on energy and a defense name and keeps rate-sensitive bets out. High-confidence calls have worked well, so I reserved that label for the single clearest cause-and-effect idea.

picks.reason: Iran-war disruption keeps crude and product prices elevated, and Valero's flexibility to run cheap heavy sour crude should widen refining margins into Q3 results.
Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, talk of heavier US strikes on Iran, and Norway's fund possibly reopening to nuclear-weapons makers all point to more demand and more buyers for defense primes.
Reuters reports US toy prices surging into the holidays because of tariffs and Iran-war shipping costs, which squeezes toymakers' margins or sales volumes.
CoreWeave sits at the center of the AI-financing scare, and a possible Fed rate hike makes its debt-funded data center build-out more expensive.
Labcorp is buying select BioReference assets for up to $872M, a large sum relative to OPKO's size that cleans up its balance sheet and the market may still be digesting.
Total flagged a quarterly profit surge driven by war-inflated energy prices, and European majors' ADRs often keep drifting higher as estimates get revised up.

watchlist_notes.note: Index is holding up (-0.1% on the day) because money is rotating out of tech into health care, staples and energy rather than leaving stocks entirely.
Most exposed to the ongoing AI-financing scare and the higher-rates reaction to hot CPI; Technology is down 5.4% on the week.
The Dow is outperforming as investors favor older-economy and defensive names over AI infrastructure plays.
Reportedly bringing a two-year-old AI feature set to China in December without the new Siri, so it stays a laggard in the AI race but is also less exposed to the AI capex unwind.
Azure past $100B and new E7 security bundles support the story, but the stock is caught in the broad tech de-rating on rate fears.
Falling with the group on worries about how AI data centers are being financed, even though Huang is still pushing engagement with Chinese AI labs.
Custom AI chips and AWS profits are the bull case, but it trades with the tech tape while rate worries compress valuations.
No major company-specific news today beyond commentary pieces; moving with the broader tech slide.
Faces a House inquiry into its $6.6B research tax credit claims days before Q3 earnings, an extra risk alongside AI spending concerns.
Unveils the next-gen Roadster tonight, a headline event that often sells off after the reveal; SpaceX's Ukraine Starlink issue is a sentiment side-note.
Higher-for-longer rates and strong bank results (Morgan Stanley, PNC beats) help net interest income, though great earnings are being punished lately.
Iran-war energy prices keep cash flow strong; analysts note the dividend is safe even if crude falls toward $79 by 2027.
Gold has two-sided drivers today: Gulf escalation supports it, but a possible Fed rate hike and rising yields work against it.
Yields slid on the tech-rout flight to safety, but hotter inflation and hike talk cap how far long bonds can rally.

top_buys.pitch: War-inflated fuel prices plus discounted heavy crude equals fat refining margins.
top_buys.why: The Iran conflict and Hormuz shipping disruption are lifting the cost of moving oil and refined products, which supports crack spreads. Valero's ability to run heavy sour barrels from Canada and Venezuela at a discount boosts that margin further. TotalEnergies already flagged a profit surge from the same backdrop, suggesting the quarter is strong across the industry. Energy was one of the better sectors last week, so this doesn't fight the tape.
top_buys.risks: If the war de-escalates or the US eases shadow-fleet sanctions enough to cut freight rates, crude and product spreads could narrow quickly.
top_buys.watch: Valero's Q3 earnings and commentary on crack spreads and heavy-crude differentials.

top_buys.pitch: Escalating Gulf conflict and a possible new sovereign-fund buyer base favor defense primes.
top_buys.why: Houthis are threatening more attacks on Saudi Arabia and the US is reportedly weighing heavier munitions against Iran, which points to replenishment orders for precision weapons. Northrop is expanding its precision weapons and counter-drone portfolio, the exact area in demand. Separately, Norway's €2 trillion fund may be allowed to own nuclear-weapons makers, a potential new flow of capital into this group.
top_buys.risks: Defense stocks have already run on war headlines, and a ceasefire or budget delay would take the air out quickly.
top_buys.watch: Northrop's upcoming quarterly results and any formal US strike decision on Iran.

top_buys.pitch: Tariffs plus war-driven shipping costs are squeezing toys right into the holiday season.
top_buys.why: Reuters reports US toy prices surging ahead of the holidays because tariffs and the Iran war are raising input and freight costs. Toymakers either eat the cost and lose margin or raise prices and lose volume, and holiday quarter is make-or-break. The market tends to underreact to this kind of slow-burning cost squeeze until guidance is cut.
top_buys.risks: Mattel has managed tariffs well before by shifting sourcing, and a strong Q3 print or a holiday demand surprise would reverse the thesis.
top_buys.watch: Mattel's Q3 earnings and any commentary on holiday pricing and freight costs.

top_buys.pitch: The most leveraged name in the AI build-out as financing fears and rate-hike talk collide.
top_buys.why: Reuters called CoreWeave the heart of the AI wipeout, with investors questioning how data center expansion is being financed. Hot September inflation has put a Fed hike back on the table, which raises the cost of the debt this business model depends on. Even blowout chip results from TSMC failed to stop the selling, a sign sentiment, not fundamentals, is driving the group lower.
top_buys.risks: These stocks are extremely volatile and a single large contract announcement or dovish Fed speaker could spark a violent bounce.
top_buys.watch: Any new AI-financing or debt-raise headlines and the next Fed meeting commentary.

top_buys.pitch: A deal worth up to $872M to a company this small can change the balance sheet story.
top_buys.why: Labcorp agreed to buy select assets of OPKO's BioReference Health for up to $872M, a meaningful amount relative to OPKO's market value. Cash from the sale reduces financing risk and lets management focus on its pharma and diagnostics pipeline. Small-cap divestitures like this often get digested over days rather than in one open.
top_buys.risks: Much of the consideration is contingent, and OPKO has a history of disappointing on its remaining pipeline, so the pop can fade fast.
top_buys.watch: Deal terms detail, closing timeline, and how management says it will use the proceeds.

summary.top_pick: Valero, because war-driven product prices plus cheap heavy sour crude should expand refining margins into earnings.
summary.watch: Watch Tesla's Roadster reveal tonight, further AI-financing headlines around CoreWeave, and any new Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure.
